Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.rt

Class HostValues

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.rt.HostValues
public final class HostValues extends Object
The rule that decides what a Java (or Kotlin) object means when a host hands it to a script.

One rule, one place, because it is applied at three doors: Runtime uses it for bind and call, api.Interop uses it for the documented bridge, and a javax.script host reaches it through the engine. If those three disagreed, the same List would be a list in one snippet and an error in another, which is the kind of thing a language never recovers from.

What crosses

  1. a value the language already understands, unchanged — identity is the point, so a host function can mutate the list its script is holding;
  2. the ordinary Java shapes Values.fromHost(java.lang.Object) widens: numbers, text, collections, arrays, maps;
  3. an enum, as its name;
  4. a function-shaped object — one public invoke method (a Kotlin lambda, a Groovy closure) or one abstract method (a java.util.function type, any single-abstract-method adapter) — as a HostFunction;
  5. nothing else.

The last row is the load-bearing decision, and it is a security decision rather than a purist one. A host could wrap an arbitrary object and let a script read its fields, and some scripting languages do; that is how a script ends up at System.out.getClass().getProtectionDomain() and how a Capabilities check is quietly bypassed. Here a Java object reaches a script only as data, as a name, or as one method the host declared — and calling that method is the whole of what the script may do with it. No field, no other method, no class object.

The reflection in this class is also deliberately narrow in a second way: it looks only at public methods of public types, and falls back to Method.setAccessible(boolean) solely so a lambda whose class is package-private (which is what Kotlin emits) can be called through the public interface it implements.

    • hostValue

      public static Object hostValue(String what, Object value)
      Converts a value for a named position: a global, an argument.

      The name is in the message because these are the two places a host gets the conversion wrong, and both are the host's own code. The rule is toMandela(java.lang.Object) itself — only the wording of the refusal differs.

      Parameters:
      what - the name or position, for the message
      value - the candidate
      Returns:
      the value the machine can run on
      Throws:
      MandelaError - when the value has no Mandela form

    • hostArgs

      args - the arguments, in any host form
      Returns:
      the arguments in Mandela form

    • tryCallable

      public static Callable tryCallable(Object value)
      Turns anything that looks like a function into a script callable, or answers null when the value is not function-shaped.

      Total by construction: a caller uses this to test a candidate and keeps its own fallback, which is what lets api.Interop refuse in its own words while sharing the same detection.

      Parameters:
      value - the candidate
      Returns:
      the callable, or null
